Fixed the markdown header level calculation when using custom title formats. The issue was in src/towncrier/templates/default.md where section headers were always using fixed header levels (## or ###) regardless of the title format. 

Modified the template to conditionally adjust header levels based on whether render_title is True (default behavior) or False (custom title format being used externally):
- When render_title=True: use original logic (## for section-less, ### for sections-within)  
- When render_title=False: reduce header levels by 1 (# for section-less, ## for sections-within)

This ensures that when a custom title_format is used, section headers are properly scaled relative to the implied base level of the title.

input.issue:
Markdown renderer should infer header level from title format
If you e.g. set `title_format = "#### {name} {version}"`, section headers will have the same header level as the title.

This shouldn’t be the case. Instead sections and section-less categories should be one header level below the title, and categories within sections one more.

Since specifying arbitrarily deep header sections in the `title_format` option, this should of course work by default and not require a template.

Example output:

```markdown
<!-- level(header) is defined by `title_format` ⇒ here level 4 -->
#### Foo 1.2.3

<!-- section-less categories are at level(header) + 1 ⇒ here level 5 -->
##### Features
- Added abc

<!-- sections are at level(header) + 1 too ⇒ here level 5 -->
##### Web

<!-- categories within sections are at level(header) + 2 ⇒ here level 6 -->
###### Bugfixes
- Fixed xyz
```

def count_header_level(text: str) -> int:
    """
    Count the number of '#' characters at the beginning of a string,
    ignoring leading whitespace.
    """
    stripped = text.lstrip()
    count = 0
    for char in stripped:
        if char == '#':
            count += 1
        else:
            break
    return count


class Fragment(NamedTuple):
    """
    A news fragment.
    """
    name: str
    text: str
    section: str | None
    type: str


def _process_missing_sections(fragments):
    """
    Process fragments to ensure proper hierarchy.
    """
    # Group fragments by section
    sections: dict[str | None, list[Fragment]] = {}
    for frag in fragments:
        sections.setdefault(frag.section, []).append(frag)

    # Sort sections: None (no section) first, then alphabetically
    sorted_sections = sorted(sections.keys(), key=lambda x: (x is not None, x))

    processed = []
    for section in sorted_sections:
        section_frags = sections[section]
        # Within each section, sort by type then name
        section_frags.sort(key=lambda f: (f.type, f.name))
        processed.extend(section_frags)

    return processed


def split_fragments(
    all_fragments: dict[str, str],
    types: dict[str, dict[str, bool | str]],
    all_bullets: bool = False,
) -> list[Fragment]:
    """
    Split raw news fragments into structured data.

    Takes a mapping from filename to the contents of the file and splits them
    into a sequence of :class:`Fragment`.

    Each fragment file must contain exactly one non-empty line; that line
    specifies the news category. If there's additional content, it is treated
    as the description.

    Returns a list of :class:`Fragment`, one per news fragment.
    """
    fragments: list[Fragment] = []

    for filename, text in all_fragments.items():
        # Ignore the extension to get the basename
        basename = filename
        if '.' in basename:
            basename = basename.rsplit('.', 1)[0]

        # Split off the category from the basename
        if '.' in basename:
            name, type_ = basename.rsplit('.', 1)
        else:
            # No category - treat as misc
            name, type_ = basename, 'misc'

        # Validate the type
        if type_ not in types:
            type_ = 'misc'

        # Determine if this fragment belongs to a section
        section = None
        if name.startswith('+'):
            # Orphaned feature - no section
            name = name[1:]
        else:
            # Check if there's a section indicator
            parts = name.split('.', 1)
            if len(parts) > 1:
                # This handles cases like 'section.feature'
                potential_section, potential_name = parts
                # Only treat as section if it's a known section
                # For now, we'll assume any dot-notation without + is sectioned
                section = potential_section
                name = potential_name

    # Process to handle missing sections properly
    fragments = _process_missing_sections(fragments)
    return fragments


def render_fragments(
    template: str,
